title: targetdir.bats:980 says the 0163 workspace case stays failed, where 0.1.8 passed it
body:
## Problem

The comment on the 0163 arm "a workspace's own target-dir = "target", over an unreadable directory beneath it, fails, saying how to clear it" (tests/unit/targetdir.bats:978-980) gives vc's ruling as "so it stays failed". That "stays" is measured against v2 of 0163's fix, which the ruling kept. Against 0.1.8 the failure is new: 0.1.8 passed this case at rc 0, clearing the config because the crate it answered builds into its own target. A reader takes "stays" against the last release. RELEASES/0.1.9.md said the same and was corrected at 891e700e, and 0163's Resolution is corrected beside this issue.

## Measured

That arm alone, in a scratch clone of d7f2ed13 with lib/ and bin/devbin checked out from v0.1.8 (lib/LICENSE.md, new in 0.1.9, left beside them): not ok at `assert_failure`, "Expected failure (non-zero exit) but got exit code 0", its walk line reading "no cargo config naming target-dir or include is in play here -- not failed". Clone: ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-vc/issues-20261007/base018.

## Fix

The comment says the case fails, and that the failure is new in 0.1.9, eg "... and only what the hole hides tells which, so it fails, where 0.1.8 cleared the config; the failure gives the remedy."

## Done when

1. The comment no longer says "stays", and the arm is otherwise unchanged.

Not swept: 0.1.9 adds 77 comment lines in lib, bin and tests that carry "stays", "still", "no longer" or "now". Most say what the code does, and none was read against 0.1.8 for this issue.

## Resolution

Landed at 6888bf18 on a green full suite (vc's, 2220 of 2220 ok, 0 not ok, .errors empty, seal 20261007-1151). The comment on 0163's arm "a workspace's own target-dir = "target", over an unreadable directory beneath it, fails, saying how to clear it" (tests/unit/targetdir.bats:978-981) now says the case fails, where 0.1.8 cleared the config, and no longer that it stays failed. "Stays" was measured against v2 of 0163's fix, which vc's ruling kept, and a reader takes it against the last release. The arm is otherwise unchanged; the comment is one line longer.

Evidence, in ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-dc/0183/runs/, at a3fcb6f5 in the scratch clone over main 45b16f3a: the targeted run (targetdir, helpers, contract, neutral, documentation, readonlygit, harness and help), 331 of 331 under BSD tools and 331 of 331 with GNU tools first on PATH, the tree clean before and after; the only skips are require_command's own two (targeted-{bsd,gnu}-20261007-100753.log).

Not swept, as the issue says: 0.1.9's other comment lines that carry "stays", "still", "no longer" or "now".
